title: Quasi-compact and quasi-separated permanence for algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Point spaces carry the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. An algebraic space is quasi-compact if its point space is quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover); it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback along every affine scheme mapping to its target has quasi-compact point space; it is quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For any morphism $f:X\to Y$, if $X$ is quasi-compact and $Y$ is quasi-separated, then $f$ is quasi-compact; if in addition $X$ is quasi-separated, then $f$ is also quasi-separated.

proof.text: Put $B=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and apply [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] with $S'=B$: replace $X,Y,f$ by $j_!X,j_!Y,j_!f$, algebraic spaces over $B$. By its part (1) every $S$-scheme atlas of $X$ stays an atlas of $j_!X$ and sheaf fibre products over $S$ go to those over $B$; the absolute diagonals of the statement are the diagonals over $B$ of these spaces. A field-valued point of $j_!X$ is a field-valued point of $X$ together with its induced map to $S$, and part (3) identifies the representable etale scheme maps to $X$ and to $j_!X$, so the final topologies of [def-a1-space-point-topology] agree and $|j_!X|=|X|$, likewise for every space over $S$. Choose an affine scheme $W$ and a representable surjective etale atlas $p:W\to X$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas], using the assumed quasi-compactness of $|X|$; by part (1) it is an atlas of $j_!X$. To show that $a_X:j_!X\to B$ is quasi-compact, let $T\to B$ be an arbitrary affine scheme test. Pulling back the one-member surjective etale family $\{W\to X\}$ along $X\times_BT\to X$, and using $(X\times_BT)\times_XW\simeq W\times_BT$, the base change $W\times_BT\to X\times_BT$ is a representable surjective etale map by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] over the base $B$.

source.place: Tag 073B (lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-permanence), proof of (1), with Z = Spec Z; atlas input: spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H6 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover).

proof.text: Write $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $W\times_BT\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}C)$, which is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The final assertion of [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas] (a representable surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme has quasi-compact target point space), applied to the atlas $W\times_BT\to X\times_BT$ of step 1, gives quasi-compactness of $X\times_BT$. Since this holds for every affine $T\to B$, it proves that $a_X$ is quasi-compact by the definition in the item.

source.place: Tag 073B (lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-permanence), proof of (1), checking quasi-compactness of X over Spec Z; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03E4 (lemma-quasi-compact-space).

proof.text: Let $a_Y:j_!Y\to B$ be the absolute structure map. Its relative diagonal is the absolute diagonal of $Y$, so the hypothesis that $Y$ is quasi-separated says exactly that $a_Y$ is quasi-separated. We have $a_Y\circ j_!f=a_X$, quasi-compact by steps 1-2. Apply [lem-sfb-space-qc-cancellation] over the base scheme $B$ to $j_!f$ and $a_Y$: $j_!f$ is quasi-compact. To return to $S$, let $T\to Y$ be an affine test over $S$; part (1) of [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] gives $j_!(X\times_YT)\simeq j_!X\times_{j_!Y}T$, and the point spaces agree as in step 1, so $X\times_YT$ has quasi-compact point space. Hence $f$ is quasi-compact, proving the first clause and the quasi-compact assertion in the second.

Assume now that $X$ is also quasi-separated. Work over $B$ as in step 1. Put $P=X\times_YX$ and $Q=X\times_BX$, using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; by part (1) of [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] $P$ is $j_!$ of the fibre product over $S$, and an affine test $T\to P$ over $S$ is the same as one over $B$, with the same point space of every pullback (step 1). For any affine scheme $T\to P$, write its two maps as $u,v:T\to X$; they satisfy $fu=fv$. On every test scheme a section of $X\times_PT$ is a pair $(x,t)$ with $x=u(t)=v(t)$. This is exactly a section of $X\times_QT$, where $T\to Q$ is induced by $(u,v)$. Thus these two sheaf fibre products are canonically isomorphic. The latter has quasi-compact point space since the absolute diagonal $X\to Q$ is quasi-compact. Consequently every affine test of the relative diagonal $X\to P$ has quasi-compact source. This proves that $f$ is quasi-separated. Together with step 3 this proves the second clause. The argument uses neither quasi-compactness of $Y$ nor affineness of intersections of opens.
